messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@edgecart.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@edgecart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Integration map + TTFT acceptance criteria & chunk cadence asks

Hi Liam / Priya — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap + clear asks so we can align internal teams and scope the pilot: 

Summary of what we heard: 
- Primary use: cart personalization + FAQ augmentation for checkout flows (short prompts, many concurrent requests).
- Target traffic for pilot: 400–800 RPS burstable; steady-state ~150 RPS.
- Important: client must see 'first useful content' quickly (decision tree highlights) so TTFT is a top priority.

Redwood proposed acceptance criteria (please confirm):
- Median TTFT <= 200 ms at steady-state 150 RPS
- p95 TTFT <= 800 ms under expected burst profile (up to 800 RPS for 30s windows)
- Sustained throughput: 1,200 tokens/sec per model instance (we'll size pools)
- Concurrency target: 200 concurrent warm sessions for pilot routing

Streaming / chunking preferences we discussed:
- We'll deliver SSE by default for browsers, WebSocket optional for mobile SDKs.
- Chunk cadence: aim for initial priming chunk within first 150–250 ms, subsequent chunks every 180–350 ms depending on response length.
- Small first chunk (20–60 bytes) to enable UX render; rest chunking prioritized by semantic boundaries where feasible.

Asks for EdgeCart (action items we need from you to finalize scope):
1) Pilot traffic sketch (CSV) with representative RPS and top 10 prompt templates — see attached pilot-traffic-profiles.csv.
2) Confirmation on client-side capability: SSE supported for checkout iframe? If not, we'll default to WebSocket.
3) Any constraints on connection lifetime (max open connections per client) and preferred TLS cipher baselines.

Next steps: 
- If you confirm acceptance criteria above, we'll produce an integration MAP (attached) and a proposed pilot schedule.
- Internal owners: Ben will handle pricing/commit; Rishi will scope infra and fallbacks; I'll lead the integration checklist with your platform team.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: integration-MAP-v1.xlsx (outline: pilot scope, ownership, dates)

Subject: Re: Integration map + TTFT acceptance criteria & chunk cadence asks

Thanks Soojin — good writeup. Quick answers inline: 

- Pilot traffic CSV received. We'll add two synthetic high-cardinality prompts (cart-abandoned and upsell-blend) and send back by EOD Friday.
- SSE is supported inside our checkout iframe in desktop; mobile clients currently prefer long-lived WebSockets. We'll confirm mobile SDK constraints by Friday too.
- Connection limits: our CDN closes idle connections after 120s; per-client open connection cap is 8. Not expected to be an issue but flagging.

Small ask: can Redwood confirm fallback behavior if TTFT exceeds p95 during a burst? Do you implement graceful degrade (shorter responses / cached templating) or model fallback?

Liam
VP Product, EdgeCart

On attachments: pilot-traffic-profiles.csv acknowledged.
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration map + TTFT acceptance criteria & chunk cadence asks

Nice summary — answering Liam's fallback question: 
- Primary fallback is model variant fallback (lower-latency quantized variant) + automatic response-length trimming when we detect token-time pressure.
- For critical short responses (decision trees) we can enable prefix caching so first chunk contains precomputed content — that reduces TTFT substantially at the cost of some cache-warm complexity.
- SLA-wise for pilot we'll document an operational fallback: if p95 breaches 900 ms for >3 minutes, switch traffic to dedicated reserved pool and notify EdgeCart via webhook + Slack incident channel.

Budget note: to meet the proposed p95 under bursts we recommend a small dedicated pool for pilot (monthly reserved for test window). I'll include pricing in the MAP and flag tradeoffs.

-Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
